title: Falcons QB depth tested early: Tagovailoa sidelined, Penix limited, Rush signed
dek: Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa is out of practice Wednesday with a tight back flare-up that the team characterizes as a recurrence of an existing injury. Backup Michael Penix Jr. remains limited after ACL surgery, prompting Atlanta to sign veteran Cooper Rush as depth insurance.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Tagovailoa will miss Wednesday's practice but is expected to return next week according to ESPN's reporting, though Penix's timeline remains uncertain pending medical clearance.
bottom_line: Tagovailoa's expected one-week absence and Penix's indeterminate clearance timeline will shape how the Falcons allocate reps in the first week of camp. Watch for updates on Penix's medical progress and whether Tagovailoa's return happens as early as ESPN's sources indicated; a longer absence or setback would pressure the organization's contingency depth more severely.
body: The Falcons are navigating a sudden quarterback shortage on the opening day of training camp, with starter Tua Tagovailoa sidelined by a recurring back injury and backup Michael Penix Jr. still recovering from ACL surgery.

Tagovailoa will not practice Wednesday due to what the team calls a tight back flare-up, according to ESPN's reporting citing sources familiar with the situation. Coach Kevin Stefanski said he expects Tagovailoa to return "sooner rather than later," and sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter that the back injury is not considered serious, with Tagovailoa expected to return next week. The quarterback had practiced in recent days without incident before the flare-up emerged.

Penix, the backup who underwent right ACL surgery in November, remains on a longer timeline. He performed individual drills and 7-on-7 work during spring practice but has not yet been cleared for 11-on-11 team sessions. Penix said the recovery could take four weeks or potentially less depending on how his body heals, and he emphasized caution given his injury history: "I have a long injury history. The last thing I want to do is rush back just to get back on the field. This is the third ACL. We're not taking it lightly." Stefanski indicated he is deferring to the medical staff on Penix's return date and is uncertain when the backup will be available.

With those two unavailable, undrafted rookie free agent Jack Strand from Division II Minnesota State Moorhead was the only quarterback fully cleared for practice on Day 1. The Falcons released veteran Trevor Siemian on Wednesday with a non-football injury designation, clearing the way for the team to add depth.

Atlanta signed 32-year-old Cooper Rush, a veteran who spent his first eight seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before appearing in four games last season with the Baltimore Ravens. The move provides the team with an experienced option while Tagovailoa and Penix are unavailable.

The situation underscores how quickly depth charts can shift during camp. Stefanski joked that Matt Ryan, now the team's president of football, will not be seeing action under center, hinting that the Falcons expect the current situation to stabilize within days rather than weeks.
